utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The Appeals Chamber is now in session, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case IT-94-1-A-R77, the Prosecutor versus Dusko Tadic, in a matter concerning allegations against prior counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: As Your Honours are aware, I appear on behalf of the interested party, Dusko Tadic. May I firstly say how grateful I am to Your Honours for allowing me just a little time this morning before Your Honours came into court. It has been helpful and useful, if I may say so. Secondly, the next witness who is to give evidence, I understand, would wish to give his evidence in closed session. There was a letter written by Mr. Livingston to the Tribunal on the 17th of November of last year indicating firstly that he wished to give his evidence in that way, and secondly indicating the reasons why he would wish to give his evidence in that way. I hope I don't need to say more than that in open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Are there any objections to the motion?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not exactly sure who the next witness is, but regardless of who that is, we would not object to a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Abell, would you like to explain a little more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I thought that placed the responsibility on you to call the name, just in case there were any difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then it is so ordered. There will be a closed session. Mr. Registrar, will you make the arrangements?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 5.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of September, 1999, at 10 a.m.
